clue.text: As tied at a 26 5?

parts.note: the cross-reference makes this a royal wedding, where the ... family ties the ..., and a groom's tie is fastened in a style named after the same family

explanation.surface: A question about how something was fastened at a royal marriage ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: The Windsors are Britain's royal family, so at their weddings a Windsor ties the knot; the answer is also a fat, formal necktie knot.
explanation.definitionFit: A necktie style named after the Duke of Windsor, fitting the pun on the royal family marrying.

clue.text: Spirit with which one's consumed by rage

indicators.note: being consumed by something means being swallowed up inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: rage means wrath
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A ghostly presence whose own character has been eaten up by fury.
explanation.definitionFit: A wraith is a ghost or apparition, a spirit of the dead.

clue.text: One fool (or two overlapping?)

parts.note: the two fools here are a nit, a simpleton

indicators.note: where two words overlap they share a letter, so the shared T is only written once

parts.note: the second of the two fools is a twit

explanation.surface: A self-deprecating aside that one idiot might be two idiots sharing a little.
explanation.walkthrough: NIT and TWIT, both meaning fool, overlap on their shared T, giving one word for a fool built from two.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitwit is a silly or foolish person, a dimwit.

clue.text: Russian claims soldier caught for term of rank

indicators.note: to claim is to take hold of, so the Russian name wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: Sergey is a typical Russian man's name
a soldier is a caste of ant
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A Russian lays claim to a soldier taken prisoner, in the language of military rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeantcy is the office or period of holding the rank of sergeant.

clue.text: One of eight, perhaps, quarrelsome type?

definitions.meaning: a member of a rowing eight pulls an oar
to row (rhyming with cow) is to quarrel, so a quarreller is jokingly one who rows

explanation.surface: A crew member who also turns out to be argumentative.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pulls an oar in a racing boat; the second sense punningly makes a brawler one who rows.

clue.text: See 26
Carefully extract bat and lion, then behead Shed!

parts.note: to bat an eyelid is to wink
Leo is the lion of the zodiac

indicators.note: to behead a word is to remove its first letter

parts.note: a shed is a hut

explanation.surface: Gruesome instructions for extracting a bat and a lion before decapitating something.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the head of HUT leaves UT; 'then' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To winkle out is to prise something out with care, like a winkle from its shell.

clue.text: It's done up and done down

indicators.note: in a down entry the word reads the same going up as coming down, a symmetrical word

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A task finished both upwards and downwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome, so in this down light it can be read up or down.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is an act, something that has been carried out.

clue.text: Boundless, popular and OK about it

parts.note: something popular is in

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for OK goes round the other piece

parts.note: OK means fine

explanation.surface: Something limitless that is both well liked and acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Infinite means without limits, endless, synonymous with boundless.

clue.text: Yellow fabric called to be woven under green light

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece written under another comes after it

parts.note: a green light is permission to go

indicators.note: weaving interlaces threads, so the letters of the word are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A gold material, named and woven beneath a green lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'under' places the jumbled letters (LDLACE, from 'to be woven') beneath the green light, so they come second.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold lace is braid or trimming made with gold thread, a yellow ornamental fabric.

clue.text: Sound to fix table

indicators.note: sound signals that the word is said aloud rather than spelled

parts.note: to fix an animal, euphemistically, is to alter (neuter) it

explanation.surface: An instruction for steadying a wobbly table.
explanation.walkthrough: Fix in the euphemistic sense of neuter a pet gives ALTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An altar is the communion table in a church.

clue.text: Composition of 18 found hot girl and went gooey

indicators.note: going gooey means melting into a sticky mess, so the letters lose their shape and reform

parts.note: the word went doubles as part of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A man melts sentimentally after discovering an attractive girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is ERIC CLAPTON, whose ballad this is; the letters of FOUND HOT GIRL plus WENT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A love song written and recorded by Eric Clapton in 1977.

clue.text: Sort of paper sees giants of literature and fantasy going head to head

indicators.note: two words meeting head to head means the first one faces backwards so their starts touch

parts.note: T. S. Eliot is a giant of literature
a troll is a giant in fantasy stories

explanation.surface: Literary and fantasy giants confront one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going head to head' turns the poet's name round (TOILE) so its first letter meets the troll's first letter; 'giants' serves both pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavatory paper, sold on a cylinder.

clue.text: Overly fussy pedestrian losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means a word drops its first letter

parts.note: pedestrian means dull, banal

explanation.surface: A dull, footslogging person who is too particular loses their head.
explanation.definitionFit: Anal, short for anal-retentive, describes someone obsessively meticulous.

clue.text: Tiny amount won, perhaps, invested in state in Scottish town

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the unit sits in the Scottish town

parts.note: Perth is a town in Scotland

indicators.note: invest can mean clothe, so the jumbled word wraps around the state
perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged another way

parts.note: NY is New York state

explanation.surface: A small lottery win put into a state scheme in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' jumbles the currency to NWO; 'invested' is used in its old sense of clothed, so those letters wrap around the state, making NNYWO.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennyworth is as much as a penny buys, so a very small quantity.

clue.text: Composition of 18 regularly dropping off

indicators.note: composition means putting together, so the letters are assembled afresh

parts.note: 18 across is the guitarist Eric Clapton

explanation.surface: A Clapton song about nodding off routinely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composition of 18' looks like 10's definition again, but here it rearranges ERIC CLAPTON.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcolepsy is a condition of repeatedly falling asleep without warning.

clue.text: Get the reason to take someone on again

parts.note: to reap is to get or gain
the point is the reason or purpose

explanation.surface: Understand the logic behind rehiring someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappoint is to give someone a post again, rehiring them.

clue.text: Achilles' heel taking some days, say, to find

indicators.note: say signals a word spoken, judged by its pronunciation

parts.note: a week is some days
to spot is to find or notice

explanation.surface: Finding a hero's vulnerable point takes a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles' heel is a vulnerability, a point of weakness.

clue.text: Railway worker crashing into lamp

indicators.note: something crashing is wrecked, so the letters are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A railwayman crashes into a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is part of the fodder, not a link: INTO plus LAMP rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilotman guides trains over single-track lines during engineering work.

clue.text: Musician having brought back passion, kid holding hand beginning to tremble

indicators.note: brought back means turned round, read in reverse

parts.note: ire is passion, anger

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece surrounds the others

parts.note: to kid is to con
to give a hand is to clap

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A performer with renewed fire, a child gripping a hand and starting to shake.
explanation.walkthrough: IRE reversed gives ERI; CON holds CLAP and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Clapton is a famous English guitarist and singer.

clue.text: This could be "Grand", as could be that

parts.note: could be is a sense of can
yon is an old word for that

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about something grand.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand Canyon is the famous gorge in Arizona.

clue.text: Setter given a pork pie and corn

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me
pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for lie

explanation.surface: Snack food: a crossword setter with a pork pie and some corn.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork pie is British rhyming slang (pork pie = lie).
explanation.definitionFit: Mealie is a South African word for maize or a corncob.

clue.text: See 1
Huge sea creature seen as we help, desperately, to protect marines

indicators.note: to protect is to surround, so the marines go inside
desperately suggests wild, disordered action, reordering the letters

parts.note: RM is the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A whale appears as volunteers frantically shield the marines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperately' rearranges AS WE HELP into SPEWHALE, which surrounds RM.
explanation.definitionFit: The sperm whale is the largest toothed whale.

clue.text: It's "frost" to sound and this you've found!

indicators.note: to sound means said aloud, judged by how it is heard

parts.note: rime is frost

explanation.surface: A clue about frost and words that chime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' and 'found' chime together, so 'this you've found' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Words with matching endings, as sound with found, form a rhyme.

clue.text: Air put in tyres on Ghia

indicators.note: put in means placed within, so the answer is found within the words

explanation.surface: Inflate the tyres on an Italian-styled car.
explanation.walkthrough: Ghia is a car-design firm, used on Ford models.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune or melody.

clue.text: Shame about old member so backward offering bombast

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so pity goes round the rest

parts.note: a shame is a pity
O is old
MP is a member of parliament

indicators.note: backward means reading the word in reverse

explanation.surface: Regret over an old member's pompous oratory.
explanation.walkthrough: SO reversed is OS; O, MP and OS go in PITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombast is pompous, inflated speech, closely related to self-important pomposity.

clue.text: Philander separated? This united them!

parts.note: split the word for a womaniser into Phil and Er, the late Prince Philip and Elizabeth Regina, joined in marriage in 1947

explanation.surface: A philanderer split apart, and a ceremony joins him up again.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen; Phil is Prince Philip.
explanation.definitionFit: The marriage of Princess Elizabeth to Philip in 1947 was a ceremony of the royal family.

clue.text: See 10
Raise each nine, not one inappropriately

indicators.note: inappropriately means arranged wrongly, so the letters are shuffled
not means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Lift each nine, though not one improperly.
explanation.walkthrough: EACH NINE without I is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance is to raise or increase in quality or value.
